name: MioIsland
summary: Puts Claude Code session status and one-click approvals in the MacBook notch — a genuinely useful ambient surface, wrapped in more whimsy than the job needs.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A human-facing macOS surface. It integrates with Claude Code through auto-installed hooks and offers a plugin system for themes, buddies and sounds, but exposes no API, CLI or MCP endpoint another agent could drive.

hlido_opinion.headline: Puts Claude Code session status and one-click approvals in the MacBook notch — a genuinely useful ambient surface, wrapped in more whimsy than the job needs.
hlido_opinion.body: MioIsland solves a small, real annoyance for anyone supervising several coding-agent sessions: you cannot tell at a glance which one is waiting for you. It turns the MacBook notch into a control centre that shows per-session status (cyan working, green done, red error), surfaces a diff with green and red highlighting when Claude needs permission so you can approve or deny without switching windows, summarises what the agent is discussing without expanding, tracks API usage against 5-hour and weekly limits, and jumps to the exact terminal tab across Ghostty, iTerm2, Warp, Terminal and others. The unattended-alert behaviour is the best-judged detail on the page — a session idle 30 seconds turns orange and 60 seconds turns red, which is the right shape for a tool whose point is that you stepped away. Zero config with auto-installed hooks and bilingual EN/zh support lower the cost of trying it. The reservations are about evidence and emphasis rather than the idea. A large share of the surface is given to a pet system (18 ASCII species, a pixel cat with six expressions), chiptune sound packs and theme plugins, which reads as a hobby project's priorities and makes the serious monitoring story harder to find. The required call-to-action check failed and there is no evidence or demo artifact we could verify beyond an animated mock, so the download is the only way to find out whether it works. There is no pricing or access statement, and nothing addresses what a notch app reading every Claude Code session can see or where that goes — for a tool sitting on top of your source edits, that silence is the real gap. Worth a try for a Mac developer already running multiple Claude Code sessions; not yet something to depend on.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) because the core monitoring, approval and jump-to-terminal behaviour is described specifically enough to evaluate, the unattended escalation timings are sensibly chosen, and the setup cost is genuinely low. It is held below VITAL because no verifiable demo or evidence artifact exists on the public surface, the required call-to-action check failed, and a tool with visibility into every agent session publishes nothing about data handling.
what_it_does_well: Surfaces per-session agent status ambiently, in a screen region that is otherwise wasted
Approve-or-deny with a visible diff without leaving the current window — the highest-value interaction here
Unattended escalation is well judged: orange at 30 seconds idle, red at 60
Tracks API usage against 5-hour and weekly windows, which is a real operational need for heavy Claude Code users
Auto-detects and jumps to the exact tab across 10+ terminal emulators
Zero config with auto-installed hooks; bilingual EN/zh following system language
iPhone companion extends the away-from-desk case the product is built around
what_it_fails_at: No verifiable demo or evidence artifact — the 'interactive demo' is an animation, so the download is the only real test
Required call-to-action check failed on the reviewed surface
No pricing, licensing or access statement
Nothing published about what the app can read from agent sessions or where that data goes
Pets, sound packs and themes occupy more of the page than the monitoring and approval features that justify it
macOS-and-notch-only by design, so the addressable audience is narrow
Plugin counts (12+ themes, 8+ buddies, 6+ sound packs) suggest an ecosystem that is still very small
best_for: Mac developers supervising several concurrent Claude Code sessions
Anyone who leaves agents running and needs to know when one is blocked
Users who keep hitting usage limits and want the burn visible
People who work across several terminal emulators and lose track of which tab holds which session
not_recommended_for: Linux and Windows users, and Macs without a notch
Environments where an app with read access to agent sessions and diffs needs a documented data posture first
Teams wanting a shared, multi-user view of agent activity rather than one developer's menu bar
Users of coding agents other than Claude Code — the integration is specific
red_flags: The app reads Claude Code session content, including code diffs, in order to display and approve them, and the public surface says nothing about what is stored, what is transmitted, or how the iPhone companion pairing is secured.
No testable artifact on the public surface: every capability is shown as an animated mock, so none of the behaviour could be verified without installing it.

compared_to.verdict_diff: MioIsland is a monitor for Claude Code, not an alternative to it. It is only worth installing if you are already running Claude Code, and ideally more than one session at a time.
opencode is a multi-model agent CLI; MioIsland's integration is Claude-Code-specific. If you have moved off Claude Code, this tool does not follow you.

evidence_urls.claim: Monitors Claude Code sessions in the MacBook notch with per-session status colours
In-notch permission approval showing a highlighted diff
Usage tracking against 5-hour and weekly API windows
Unattended alerting escalates at 30 and 60 seconds idle
Terminal jump across Ghostty, iTerm2, Warp, Terminal and 10+ others
